properties.name: Aimere → Mataloko
properties.resupply_notes: Mataloko: basic resupply, geothermal hot springs, the St Yohanes Berchmans seminary.

properties.name: Bajawa → Bena (via Luba, Tololela, Gurusina)
water_points: Kiosks in the villages along the way; nothing guaranteed
properties.resupply_notes: Bena has minimal resupply (homestay economy); real resupply is Bajawa before or Aimere after.
hazards: Fire risk in the thatched-roof villages (Gurusina burned in 2018) — rider briefing should cover stove/flame discipline
properties.cultural_notes: Ngada megalithic villages: Bena (nine clans, ngadhu/bhaga shrines), Luba (four clans, quieter), Tololela (steep hillside, fewer visitors), Gurusina (rebuilt after the 2018 fire). Cultural-checkpoint agreements required with each village council before race day (design rule 5).
open_questions: Which of Bena/Luba/Tololela/Gurusina will actually host a checkpoint, and under what terms? (route-concept open question 2, priority 1)

properties.name: Bena → Aimere (Inerie shoulder, HAB)
properties.resupply_notes: Aimere is a basic south-coast port resupply.
hazards: Steep, loose volcanic soil on the shoulder descent; exposure in places (route-concept HAB inventory: 5–10 km)
properties.cultural_notes: Inerie is treated by the villages beneath it less as scenery than as a presiding relative; the ngadhu/bhaga shrines of Bena and Luba face its slope.
open_questions: Is the Bena→Aimere descent safe with a loaded bike? (route-concept open question 4, priority 1)

properties.name: Bena → Aimere (Inerie full circuit, Ultra)
properties.direction_note: Ultra-variant alternative to the Inerie shoulder traverse (variant A): a longer circuit around the mountain's western and southern base instead of the direct HAB shortcut over the shoulder (+40-60 km per the route concept).
water_points: Unreliable; villages on the circuit are not individually documented
properties.resupply_notes: Same endpoints as variant A; nothing new confirmed on the circuit itself.
hazards: Wholly conceptual; no source describes this specific circuit track
properties.cultural_notes: Passes close to Wolobobo Hill (p-wolobobo), a sunrise viewpoint over Inerie and the Bajawa plateau.
open_questions: Unscouted; only proposed as an Ultra-variant distance-adder, not evaluated for track existence.

properties.name: Blidit → Waiterang (Egon ascent and descent, HAB)
water_points: None above Blidit; carry full capacity
properties.resupply_notes: Waiterang has a small dive resort scene, no confirmed shop resupply.
hazards: Active fumaroles at the crater; PVMBG Level I (Normal) as of mid-2026 monitoring reports, but a safety briefing (no lingering near fumaroles) is required before any ascent
properties.cultural_notes: Egon is this section's hike-a-bike centrepiece, in the same register as Kelimutu and Inerie further west (route-concept HAB inventory: 4–6 km from Blidit).
open_questions: Confirm current trail condition and fumarole safety before committing riders.

properties.name: Boawae → Mbay (Aesesa valley)
properties.resupply_notes: Mbay: full resupply, Nagekeo Regency capital.
properties.cultural_notes: The Aesesa plain is the largest rice-growing lowland on Flores (p-aesesa-plains).
open_questions: Mbay's town-centre coordinate is unverified (placed on the coastal plain near the river mouth); confirm with a field GPS fix.

properties.name: Boawae → Nangaroro (direct, skips Mbay)
properties.direction_note: Route-level alternative to the two-hop Boawae→Mbay→Nangaroro corridor, not a same-endpoint variant of a single segment: shorter and less remote per the route concept, but skips Mbay's resupply and the Aesesa plain entirely.
water_points: Unconfirmed — this line has not been desk-checked against any track source
properties.resupply_notes: None between Boawae and Nangaroro on this line.
hazards: Wholly conceptual: no source describes an existing direct track
open_questions: Does a rideable direct track exist here at all, or is Mbay unavoidable? (section 06/07 alternative named in the route concept)

properties.name: Bola → Watublapi
properties.resupply_notes: Watublapi (see s-watublapi-blidit-a) is the next resupply.

properties.name: Borong → Elar (Manggarai Timur interior)
water_points: Not documented at all — the real scouting work
properties.resupply_notes: Elar: camat office, health centre, schools only.
hazards: Genuinely unscouted interior; tracks in this area are not desk-verified against any track source
open_questions: Do rideable tracks exist through this interior at all? This is the least-known corridor in the whole concept.

properties.name: Denge → Wae Rebo (porters' trail, HAB)
water_points: A spring is reported partway up the porters' trail (unverified); carry full capacity from Denge
properties.resupply_notes: None on the trail; Wae Rebo's homestay system feeds and houses every arrival.
hazards: Steep porters' path with steps; can be greasy in light rain even in the dry season
properties.cultural_notes: Wae Rebo is the flagship cultural checkpoint of the whole course: fixed homestay/guest-fee system, a welcome ceremony expected on arrival, and a race-specific agreement with the village council is required before any checkpoint is confirmed (see p-wae-rebo).
open_questions: Which villages will host cultural checkpoints, under what terms? (Wae Rebo council agreement not yet negotiated)

properties.name: Detusoko → Moni
properties.resupply_notes: Moni: guesthouses and warungs, the usual overnight base before Kelimutu.
properties.cultural_notes: Wologai (p-wologai), an ~800-year-old Lio village, sits in the hills near this corridor as a highlight, though not directly on this line.

properties.name: Dintor → Denge (Wae Rebo trailhead)
water_points: Denge has kiosks and homestays for trekkers waiting to start the Wae Rebo trail
properties.resupply_notes: Denge is the last resupply before the Wae Rebo trailhead.
properties.cultural_notes: Follows the same coastal track described for Wae Nakeng-Nangalili-Borik-Dintor-Denge in scouting sources; not yet field-verified.
open_questions: Is this the same farm track used by trekking guides, or does the race need its own line?

properties.name: Elar → Pota (rejoining the north coast)
properties.resupply_notes: Pota (see s-pota-riung-a) is the next resupply.
open_questions: Same as the Borong→Elar leg: unscouted.

properties.name: Ende → Detusoko
properties.resupply_notes: Detusoko: basic resupply, homestays, tourism village.
properties.cultural_notes: Detusoko's rice terraces (p-detusoko-rice-terraces) are a cool, working highland landscape.

properties.name: Iteng → Ruteng
water_points: Reliable once within a few km of Ruteng
properties.resupply_notes: Ruteng is the best full resupply of the whole west region: market, hospital, banks, many hotels.
hazards: ~1,100 m of climbing from the coast; heat lower down, cold rain higher up are both plausible in the same day
properties.cultural_notes: Ruteng Cathedral and Golo Curu viewpoint sit right at the town; Cancar's spider-web rice fields (p-cancar-lingko) are a short, no-HAB side trip west of town if the schedule allows.

properties.name: Kelimutu → Wolojita
properties.resupply_notes: Wolojita: minimal, homestays.
properties.cultural_notes: Wolojita is an ikat-weaving village and district centre between Jopu and Nggela.

properties.name: Koka → Sikka (inland of the bay)
properties.resupply_notes: None named between Koka and Sikka; both ends are minimal.
hazards: A straight line between these two villages crosses open water (a south-coast bay/inlet); this sketch bulges north onto the hillside road instead, consistent with the DEM

properties.name: Labuan Bajo → Sano Nggoang via Mbeliling forest
water_points: Werang and roadside kiosks are the last reliable water before the lake; carry extra through the forest reserve
properties.resupply_notes: Full resupply in Labuan Bajo; nothing until Werang beyond a few kiosks near the forest edge.
hazards: Coordinates for Cunca Rami are unverified (needs a field GPS fix); dry-season forest track condition unknown
properties.cultural_notes: Mbeliling forest reserve is an Important Bird Area (Flores hanging parrot, monarch, crow, owl); no settlement inside the reserve to negotiate with, but track use should stay on existing paths.
open_questions: Is the forest track rideable end-to-end, or does it require dismounts near Cunca Wulang/Cunca Rami?
Confirm Cunca Rami's location with a field GPS fix (desk position and DEM elevation disagree by ~400 m).

properties.name: Lela → Maumere
properties.resupply_notes: Maumere: full resupply, Sikka Regency capital, hospital, airport.
hazards: 1992 earthquake/tsunami awareness note for the whole north coast (no route dependency)
properties.cultural_notes: Passes close to Ledalero Seminary (p-ledalero-seminary), one of the largest Catholic seminaries in the world. Wuring, the Bajo stilt village, sits a few km west of the town centre.

properties.name: Liang Bua → Reo
properties.resupply_notes: Reo is a full basic resupply: market, bank, health centre.

properties.name: Mataloko → Boawae (via Wogo)
properties.resupply_notes: Boawae: basic resupply on the Trans-Flores highway.
hazards: Ebulobo's PVMBG bulletin should be rechecked before race day (Level I/Normal as of mid-2026, but the 15 Aug 2026 M7.7 Flores earthquake triggered summit-area landslides)
properties.cultural_notes: Old Wogo's megalith complex sits ~1.5 km off the road on foot, a possible no-HAB side highlight.

properties.name: Maumere → Bola (Bola coast loop)
properties.resupply_notes: Bola: minimal resupply, south-coast kecamatan capital.
properties.cultural_notes: Ultra-variant loop named in the route concept: Maumere→Bola→Watublapi→Egon instead of the direct Maumere→Watublapi hop (+50–70 km).

properties.name: Maumere → Watublapi
properties.resupply_notes: Watublapi: minimal, homestays, ikat-weaving cooperative.
properties.cultural_notes: Watublapi is Sikka's ikat-weaving hamlet; protocol is closer to a working craft cooperative than a customary adat community — comparatively easy to arrange as a stop (p-watublapi-weaving).

properties.name: Mbay → Nangaroro (crossing the island's waist)
water_points: Unreliable; Nangaroro has homestays but water is flagged unreliable in its node record
properties.resupply_notes: Nangaroro: basic resupply, farming/fishing villages.
open_questions: Which ridge crossings between coasts exist as footpaths here — this is the narrowest waist of the island (route-concept open question 6).

properties.name: Moni → Kelimutu (dawn checkpoint)
water_points: None at the summit car park; carry from Moni
properties.resupply_notes: None beyond Moni.
hazards: Standing safety rules apply regardless of alert level: no crater-rim approach (especially Kawah II, phreatic-eruption risk), no camping in the craters; PVMBG held Kelimutu at Level I/Normal as of 5 Aug 2026
properties.cultural_notes: Kelimutu is the one non-negotiable stop of the race: riders required at the viewpoint at dawn. Paved to the car park, then stairs — treated as a short hike-a-bike, not a ridden section. In Lio belief the three lakes are where souls go after death.

properties.name: Nangaroro → Penggajawa (Blue Stone beach)
properties.resupply_notes: Minimal; no lodging confirmed at Penggajawa.
properties.cultural_notes: Penggajawa's Blue Stone (Batu Biru) beach is a classic overland-route photo stop (p-penggajawa).

properties.name: Nggela → Koka (via Paga)
water_points: Unreliable; a beach resort or two near Koka/Paga
properties.resupply_notes: Paga and Koka are day-stop/checkpoint only — no confirmed lodging.
properties.cultural_notes: Koka and Paga are twin south-coast beaches; both nodes' coordinates are unverified and flagged for a field GPS fix.
open_questions: Confirm Paga and Koka's exact coordinates in the field; the two are less than 1 km apart in the desk data.

properties.name: Penggajawa → Ende
properties.resupply_notes: Ende: full resupply, hospital, airport — the largest town of central Flores.
hazards: Iya volcano sits immediately south of the town (PVMBG Level II/Waspada, 2 km exclusion radius as of May 2026); no route dependency but worth a standing check
properties.cultural_notes: Ende is Sukarno's 1934–38 exile town: the exile house (p-sukarno-exile-house) and the Contemplation Park breadfruit tree (p-pancasila-tree) where he is said to have shaped the Pancasila.

properties.name: Pota → Riung
properties.resupply_notes: Riung has small shops and a market; nothing named en route.
hazards: Same savanna/heat/water constraints as the Reo–Pota leg; coastal headlands where the track may die (route-concept HAB inventory)
open_questions: Where does the coastal track die between Pota and Riung, and what replaces it — beach walking, a headland footpath, or a boat portage?

properties.name: Ranamese → Liang Bua
properties.resupply_notes: Small vendor stalls at the Liang Bua site only.
properties.cultural_notes: Liang Bua is the deep-time anchor of the whole race: the cave where Homo floresiensis was excavated in 2003 (see p-liang-bua).
open_questions: This descent doubles back near Ruteng rather than a direct line; confirm whether a more direct farm track exists.

properties.name: Reo → Pota (north coast savanna)
water_points: Not documented; this is the single biggest water-planning gap on the whole course
properties.resupply_notes: Pota has a parish, health centre, bank unit, schools; nothing named between Reo and Pota.
hazards: Heat, dry lontar-palm savanna, no confirmed shade or water sources along this stretch
open_questions: Is there a continuous rideable/walkable corridor Reo→Pota→Riung along or near the north coast, and where is water? (route-concept open question 1, priority 1)

properties.name: Riung → Soa (Mengeruda hot springs)
water_points: Mengeruda hot springs (not drinking water, but a landmark/rest stop) just before Soa
properties.resupply_notes: Soa is minimal (airfield only); the real resupply is Bajawa, one hop further.
hazards: ~1,300 m of climbing from the coast to the plateau in one hop
open_questions: Which ridge crossings between coasts exist as footpaths here? The DEM suggests a rideable ridge line; the track network layer is the starting point (route-concept open question 6).

properties.name: Ruteng → Borong (Manggarai Timur interior loop)
properties.resupply_notes: Borong: full resupply, market, hospital, banks, hotels.
properties.cultural_notes: Ultra-variant loop, named in the route concept as an alternative to the direct Liang Bua→Reo→Pota corridor: Ruteng→Borong→Elar→Pota (+120–160 km, very remote, unknown tracks).
open_questions: Unscouted; the whole loop needs a first field trip before it can be more than a concept sketch.

properties.name: Ruteng → Ranamese (Poco Ranaka flank)
water_points: A warung is reported at the Ranamese lakeside car park
properties.resupply_notes: None beyond the Ranamese warung; last real resupply is Ruteng.
hazards: Road climbs past 1,400–1,500 m on the Poco Ranaka flank; cold and wet at dawn even in the dry season
open_questions: Is there a farm-track alternative to the paved road over this pass, per design rule 1 (prefer the small track)?

properties.name: Sano Nggoang lakeshore → Werang
water_points: Sano Nggoang hot springs and lakeside kiosks
properties.resupply_notes: Werang is the practical resupply stop after the lake: parish, camat office, kiosks.
properties.cultural_notes: Sano Nggoang is a live site for geothermal-exploration debate locally; nothing route-relevant, but worth the organisers staying informed rather than taking a side.
open_questions: Homestay capacity at Sano Nggoang for race-week volume is unconfirmed.

properties.name: Sikka → Lela
water_points: Unreliable in Sikka/Lela; reliable once close to Maumere
properties.resupply_notes: Lela: basic resupply.
properties.cultural_notes: Sikka village and its 1899 church (p-sikka-church) are the clearest single point of contact with five centuries of Indo-Portuguese history on the island; a working village and parish, not a museum.
open_questions: Confirm Sikka village's exact coordinates in the field (desk position shifted ~1.3 km from the inland kecamatan centroid to the coast).

properties.name: Soa → Bajawa
properties.resupply_notes: Bajawa: full resupply, hotels, market, ATMs.

properties.name: Talibura → Larantuka (north-coast corridor, concept A)
water_points: Unreliable; carry capacity for the whole stretch
properties.resupply_notes: Boru (not on this line) is the nearest resupply if needed; otherwise nothing until Larantuka.
hazards: Lewotobi Laki-laki/Perempuan: PVMBG Level III (Siaga), 5 km exclusion radius as of late Aug 2026; this line stays well north of both vents by design — reconfirm PVMBG status monthly and keep the pre-agreed reroute/abort rule live
properties.cultural_notes: Primary concept line for the crux logistics question of the race: how to pass Lewotobi. Treats the whole complex as a no-go zone per design rule 6.
open_questions: What is the realistic corridor and the abort plan around Lewotobi? (route-concept open question 5, priority 1 in practice)

properties.name: Talibura → Larantuka (highway corridor via Boru, concept B)
properties.direction_note: Only usable if PVMBG status allows: this line passes within roughly the exclusion radius of the Lewotobi complex via Boru (~8 km from the vents per n-boru). Concept A (north-coast corridor) is the primary route.
properties.resupply_notes: Boru: basic resupply, PVMBG Lewotobi observation post nearby.
hazards: Passes close to the Lewotobi exclusion zone — PVMBG Level III (Siaga) as of late Aug 2026; use only with an explicit go/no-go decision on race week, and a live abort rule
open_questions: What PVMBG status level, if any, would make this corridor acceptable, and who makes that call on race week?

properties.name: Todo → Iteng
water_points: Iteng has a market (pasar Iteng) and a health centre
properties.resupply_notes: Iteng is the practical resupply between Todo and Ruteng.
properties.cultural_notes: Todo is the former seat of the Manggarai kingdom; a living village, guests received by elders, no cultural-checkpoint agreement negotiated yet (see p-todo-village).
open_questions: Confirm terms for a Todo checkpoint stop with the village council.

properties.name: Wae Rebo → Todo (onward ridge trail, concept)
properties.resupply_notes: None; Todo has a few day-trip vendor stalls only.
hazards: Onward trail condition beyond Wae Rebo is unconfirmed in any source consulted; treat as unscouted
properties.cultural_notes: If this ridge trail is not passable with a loaded bike, use s-wae-rebo-todo-b (out-and-back via Denge) instead.
open_questions: Is the Wae Rebo onward trail passable with a bike, or is it an out-and-back? (design rule / open question 3 of the route concept)

properties.name: Wae Rebo → Todo (out-and-back via Denge)
properties.direction_note: Fallback alternative: descend the porters' trail back to Denge the way you came (same HAB as the ascent), then take the Denge–Todo road east.
water_points: Denge kiosks on the way back down
properties.resupply_notes: Same as variant A once past Denge; Todo itself has no lodging.
hazards: Adds real distance and a full trail re-descent — only use if the onward trail (variant A) is confirmed impassable
properties.cultural_notes: Safety fallback named explicitly in the route concept for section 02.
open_questions: Needs a scouting verdict on variant A before this fallback can be ruled in or out as the primary line.

properties.name: Waiterang → Talibura
properties.resupply_notes: Talibura: basic resupply, easternmost kecamatan capital of Sikka Regency.
properties.cultural_notes: Talibura has a mangrove-lined shore (Desa Darat Pantai).
open_questions: Both Waiterang's and Talibura's coordinates are approximate/unverified; confirm with a field GPS fix.

properties.name: Watublapi → Blidit (Egon trailhead)
properties.resupply_notes: None; Blidit is a trailhead only.

properties.name: Werang → Dintor
water_points: Unreliable below Werang; carry capacity for the whole descent
properties.resupply_notes: Nothing named between Werang and Dintor; Dintor itself is minimal (a few kiosks).
hazards: Both Dintor's and this descent track's exact line are unverified (field:pending on n-dintor)
open_questions: Confirm the descent track/farm-road line with a field GPS trace; Dintor's coordinates are a reasoned placement, not a source pin.

properties.name: Wolojita → Nggela
properties.resupply_notes: Nggela: minimal, homestays.
hazards: A landslide has been known to cut this coastal road after heavy rain (p-wolojita)
properties.cultural_notes: Nggela is a Lio ikat-weaving village and a proposed cultural checkpoint (design rule 5); almost every household keeps a back-strap loom.
open_questions: Which villages will host cultural checkpoints, under what terms? (route-concept open question 2, priority 1)
